name: Tsung Shap
description: Tsung Shap (Disputing Tens) is a Chinese domino game adapted for cards. 2 players capture pairs of identical cards and sets of 3 cards summing to multiples of 10 from the ends of a row. Pairs score 10x pip value. Sweeps score 40 bonus. Can be played with standard card deck using Fishing mechanics.
deck: 32 Chinese dominoes or adapted standard deck

history.origins: Tsung Shap was reported by Stewart Culin in Chinese Games With Dice And Dominoes (1895), describing games played by Chinese labourers in the USA. The name means disputing tens. It uses one set of 32 Chinese dominoes as a two-player fishing game, with tiles in a row and captures from the ends.
timeline: 1895: Documented in Stewart Culin's Chinese Games With Dice And Dominoes.
history.evolution: Can be adapted for standard playing cards.

rules.objective: Score more points than the opponent by capturing pairs of identical tiles (ten times pip value), triplets that sum to a multiple of ten (pip total), and sweeps (last two table tiles for 40 bonus).
rules.gameplay: Row of tiles on table. Draw and capture from ends. Identical pair = capture (score 10x pips). Triplet summing to 10 = capture. Sweep (take last 2) = 40 bonus. Missed captures can be claimed by opponent.

strategy.advanced: Track remaining tiles. Force opponent into poor positions.

scoring.description: Pairs = 10 x pip value. Triplets by pip count. Sweeps = 40 bonus.
